audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer reads Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Fizz, Fizz, Irelia. Worse, phases[4].why and phases[5].why described Irelia winning those two stages while win[4] and win[5] say Fizz — the row and the sentence under it argued.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly, so the full layer was the stale half in both side and prose.
audit.corrected: Sides moved onto the content values, ratings for the two Fizz stages dropped to 4/10, and both whys rewritten to describe Fizz winning them.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and first-item spikes had no numbers and the level-6 phase text claimed Irelia's all-in 'caps' there.
audit.why: Chum the Waters is 120/100/80s at 1300 range, slows, then knocks up. Playful / Trickster is 16/14/12/10/8s of untargetability. Seastone Trident falls to a 3s auto-reset. Those numbers are why 6 and item-1 belong to Fizz and why the second item comes back to Irelia.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into the spikes, phases and cooldowns fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: Urchin Strike was never mentioned anywhere in the matchup, Seastone Trident's auto-attack reset was never mentioned, and Fizz's passive damage reduction was absent.
audit.why: Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s that applies on-hit — it is his gap-closer, not an escape. Seastone Trident is an auto-reset whose wind-up is the burst tell. Nimble Fighter gives flat damage reduction from all sources, which blunts Irelia's chip. Irelia's E stun is the answer to the hop's landing, and R should never be spent while he is airborne and untargetable.
audit.corrected: All three written in; 'never spend E or R into the hop' stated explicitly.

audit.why: Playful / Trickster 16s->8s, Urchin Strike 8s, Seastone Trident 7s->3s, Chum the Waters 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim.

edits.before: The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: He is untargetable for the whole hop and it is 16s at rank 1 — bait it with a Q, then spend the stun and the four stacks.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.

edits.before: - Fizz Playful / Trickster: matchup-defining — The untargetable hop dodges your whole combo — bait it before spending your burst. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Playful / Trickster is 16s at rank 1 and 8s maxed, and he is untargetable in the air — never spend your E or your R into the hop. - Urchin Strike is his 8s gap-closer at 550 range. - Seastone Trident falls to a 3s auto-reset. - Chum the Waters is 120s.

edits.before: Fizz wins by landing Playful / Trickster, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Fizz wins by sticking Chum the Waters from 1300 range, hopping untargetable through your stun, and bursting on the way down.

edits.before: If Fizz takes first blood, tighten up: Playful / Trickster is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Fizz takes first blood, stop stepping up while Playful / Trickster is available — untargetability beats any burst you own. Farm what Bladesurge can reach and re-enter only with the hop and his 120s ultimate both spent.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by making him spend the hop first: bait Playful / Trickster with a Q, then four stacks and an E-stun end him.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, E-stun the carries, and let R's wall slow whoever peels.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Fizz's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, keep the wave on him: he cannot farm inside 600 range, and his hop is 16s while your Bladesurge refunds.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions — every one is a dash and the crash is an all-in announcement you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane — no minions, no dashes, no Irelia. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions between you and him — each is a Bladesurge and the crash is an all-in you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane, where Urchin Strike still reaches you and nothing reaches him. Crash timing: crash while Playful / Trickster is down — buy a plate, a reset, or a roam.

edits.before: Fizz has no real punish for aggressive melee engage at level 1 given his poke's mana cost and cooldown, so early levels favour you
edits.after: Fizz has no punish for aggressive melee engage at level 1 and his flat damage reduction doesn't stop four stacks, so this is yours

edits.before: Fizz's Seastone Trident poke needs him in melee range without Playful/Trickster up, so a level 3 all-in while his E is on cooldown punishes him before he has real burst.
edits.after: Seastone Trident only bites from melee and Playful/Trickster is a 16s cooldown at rank 1, so a level 3 all-in while the hop is down punishes him before real burst exists.

edits.before: Chum the Waters lands a slow-and-burst combo that flips fights hard once he hits 6 — his E dodges your Q reset window, making him genuinely dangerous to engage.
edits.after: Chum the Waters slows from 1300 range then knocks you up into his full combo at 6, and the hop dodges whatever you saved to answer it — this is where the lane turns.

edits.before: Fizz is squishy and has no real answer to sustained melee pressure before his ultimate — his Seastone Trident poke has both mana cost and cooldown, and if he whiffs Playful/Trickster you can walk in and punish immediately. Push the wave and force trades whenever his E is down; he has nothing else to stop your dash-based aggression pre-6. Keep engaging on cooldown through levels 1-5 while his kit is still incomplete.
edits.after: Fizz is squishy and has no real answer to sustained melee pressure before his ultimate — Seastone Trident only bites from melee range, and if he burns Playful/Trickster you get 16s to walk in and punish immediately. Push the wave and force trades whenever the hop is down; Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash through you, not an escape, so it doesn't save him. Keep engaging on cooldown through levels 1-5 while his kit is incomplete.

edits.before: Level 6 flips this hard — Chum the Waters lands a slow that sets up a full burst combo, and his E lets him dodge your engage or your Q reset entirely, making him genuinely threatening in an all-in. This power spike carries into his first item too, where Nashor's or Riftmaker gives him burst plus an untargetable window that wins most extended fights. Play cautiously here: bait his E before committing, and don't force fights immediately after he hits 6 or backs for his first item.
edits.after: Level 6 flips this hard — Chum the Waters sticks from 1300 range, slows you and knocks you up into the full combo, and the hop dodges whatever you saved to answer it. That spike carries into his first item, where Nashor's or Riftmaker turns a 3s Seastone Trident into real damage on top of the untargetable window. Play cautiously: bait the 16s hop with a Q before committing, never spend Vanguard's Edge while he is airborne, and don't force right after he hits 6 or backs.

edits.before: Once you close the item gap with a second component, your raw stats and all-in speed start beating his burst-and-dodge combo again — Fizz falls off relative to a scaling diver once neither of you has a pure level/item lead. Look for fights where his E is down or he's already used Chum the Waters, and re-assert your dive pattern; the late game swings back in your favour if you play around his cooldowns.
edits.after: Once you close the item gap with a second component, your raw stats and all-in speed start beating his burst-and-dodge combo again — Fizz falls off relative to a scaling diver once neither of you holds a level or item lead. Look for fights where the 8s hop is on cooldown or Chum the Waters' 80s is already spent, and re-assert your dive pattern; the late game swings back to you if you play around his cooldowns.

edits.before: Poke safely with Trident range advantage before committing
edits.after: Trade with a 3s Seastone Trident reset and then hop out
